title: test(spec): the third data/ file group's test titles state each cited decision in words instead of a tracker number (stage 17)
body:
Part of #20749
Clause-②: no

Stage 17 of this card: the next area of class (e), the test strings shipped under `packages/spec/src`, as ruled in `5902360492` on #20513. This stage takes the third name-ordered file group directly under `packages/spec/src/data/`: the 20 test files from `filter-comparand-type.test.ts` to `filter-view-operator-parity.test.ts`. They carried 95 messages and 99 tracker ids, citing 36 records. Every one of those ids now either states what its record decided, in words (form D), or is dropped where the title already says it. Text only: no assertion, identifier, test count or code comment changes.

## Census at the base (`2799155678`)

Instruments: `census10.cjs` (md5 `9d08602ab972b4b8643c90d64d40fa41`), `census.cjs` (md5 `6e42a45a926d375013c32d62f16a296e`), `census-wide.cjs` (md5 `c98410a19529c439adb0afbfb00026a2`) and `dirtable.cjs` (md5 `dda605c54745b4a60cc14c9a686e4eff`). They are byte-identical to the copies stages 10 to 16 used. A literal counts as a test title when its folded message is argument 0 of a `describe` / `it` / `test` call, `.each` / `.skip` / `.only` chains included. Everything else is an "other" string.

Both instruments read **1140 messages / 1207 ids in 245 files**, the seat's reading at `2799155678`. That is stage 16's head reading (1137 / 1204) plus the three ids that PRs #21819 and #21825 added in new `ui/` test titles, which ride the `ui/` stages.

## How the area was chosen

`data/` has no subdirectory to split by, so its stages take name-ordered file groups near the ~100-id bound. Stage 16's re-cut named this group at 99, and this census reads 99, so the rule needed no re-cut.

**Named for the next stages** (re-cut from the head census, 1045 / 1108; `data/` 185 / 200 left, the same cut stages 15 and 16 named):
- `data/` in two more stages, name-ordered:
  1. `filter.test.ts` to `object.test.ts`: 17 files, 103 messages / 114 ids. `object.test.ts` alone carries 42, so no cut lands nearer the bound;
  2. `query-transport.test.ts` to `validation.test.ts` (11 files, 34 / 34) with `data/driver/` (7 files, 48 / 52): 86 ids.
- `ui/` 419, about four stages. `api/` 201, two. `system/` 165, two. The files directly in `src/`, 120, one.
- The three docblock needles (`ai/build-progress.test.ts:236`, `:237`, `contracts/approval-service.test.ts:274`), one stage with their docblocks.

## What each id became

20 literals (23 ids) now state a decision in words. 3 literals (4 ids) get their subject back in words where the number stood in for it. 72 literals (72 ids) drop a number the title already explains.

Every cited record was read with its comments through REST: 35 answer 200. #14426 answers 404, and its decision was read from what landed: commit `40a44b91b` and its CHANGELOG entry (the `undefined` comparand refusal names the null predicate by its full spellings, so following it never lands in another refusal). The title already says that, so the number is dropped.

| record(s) | literal (under `data/`) | now reads |
|:--|:--|:--|
| #7872 | `filter-comparand-type.test.ts:41` | "the accepted set — one set, defined at the shared door for every driver". The ruling put the comparand-type set at the shared compile face, the measured superset, instead of per-driver policy. |
| #5869 | `filter-comparand-type.test.ts:255` | "does not judge a non-array list-operator comparand — that SHAPE is refused 400 by the engine’s shape gate". The record's 500 became an enveloped 400 at the engine's list-shape gate. |

| #20336 (2) | `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.test.ts:59`, `:174` | "the numeric grammar — a JSON number literal naming a finite double" and "numberComparandDoorVerdict — a numeric string narrows to its number, a non-numeric one is refused". |
| #20510 | `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.test.ts:308` | "`aggregated` and `boundByDriver` — the refusal says only what is true at its position". The refusal names an aggregated column as such, and names the PostgreSQL server error only where the driver binds. |
| #5701, #3948, #6520 | `filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts:82`, `:89` | One declared expect message: "(measured when $icontains was staged — a dropped predicate WIDENS, which on an RLS read scope is an unauthorized read)" and "Admitting $icontains with an arm on every JS face, in one PR, is the worked example of the clearing direction." |
| #4706 | `filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts:121` | "covers the operators retired when `$icontains` replaced `$regex`". Option B: `$regex` retired, `$icontains` added. |
| #8793 | `filter-preset-comparand.test.ts:31` | "FilterConditionSchema — a bare preset name in an ordering comparand is refused at publish". |

| #18113 | `filter-text-comparand.test.ts:51` | "isRefusedTextComparand — the one predicate every face reads, driven through every FILTER_TEXT_CASES case". Ruling D: the predicate lives with the contract's owner. |
| #4706 | `filter-text-conformance.test.ts:162` | A declared expect message: "a case-folding $contains returns both — the answer ruled out when $contains was declared case-sensitive". The record's second question, answered A. |
| #15661 | `filter-text-operator-declared-type.test.ts:184` | "textOperatorDoorVerdict — a text operator over a type that never stores a string is refused". C-deny. |

**Subject restored (4 ids):** #5222 and #7597 at `filter-comparand-type.test.ts:225` ("leaves a FieldReference alone at every position — cross-field push-down, scalar comparison and the `$eq` lowering own its fate"), #8296 at `filter-dotted-head.test.ts:40` ("a virtual head is refused: the unmaterializable-field verdict finally reaching the dotted spelling") and #19514 at `filter-save-door-face-parity.test.ts:743` ("… and the text-comparand arm stays silent").

- **The `§1` … `§7` markers stay.** They number each file's own sections, which its comments (`// §1 …`) and header name; only the card number in front of them goes.
- **Files that carried a record as a file-wide tag** (`filter-cross-field-comparison-class`, `filter-number-comparand-declared-type`, `filter-text-operator-declared-type`, `filter-like-wire-lowering`, `filter-text-comparand`): the verdict's describe now states the decision (above). The others name the contract part they pin (the judged fields, the refusal message, the fixture, the case table), and their child titles state what each part does. The files' header comments still name the records; comments are not touched here.
- **Declared labels and messages:** the five `filter-lowering.test.ts` `NULL_ROWS` names feed `it(row.name)` and the seven `filter-save-door-face-parity.test.ts` labels feed a `%s` title; vitest prints both whole, as the head run's names show.

## Text-only proof

2. **Comments:** every comment, byte-equal.
3. **Strings:** each changed string leaf must sit in a test-call title position or on a declared line, must carry a tracker id before, and must carry no `#` plus digits after. The declared lines are `filter-lowering.test.ts:81`, `:83`, `:85`, `:93` and `:95`, `filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts:82` and `:89`, `filter-save-door-face-parity.test.ts:308`, `:309`, `:311` to `:314` and `:743`, and `filter-text-conformance.test.ts:162`.

- **Result:** 20 of 20 files SAME on all three legs, with the per-file counts predicted in writing before the run.
- **Totals:** 96 changed string leaves in 95 literals, 81 titles and 15 declared. The diff's `+` and `-` lines are exactly the 96 planned lines, and every file keeps its line count.
- **Controls (10 of 10 as predicted, on scratch copies, each anchor hit once):** identifier rename DIFF; numeric literal DIFF; comment edit COMMENT DIFF; a non-title string given an id VIOLATION; a rewritten title given a new id VIOLATION; a title that was id-free at base edited VIOLATION; one title reverted to base SAME; a declared string given a new id VIOLATION; an undeclared `expect` message changed VIOLATION; a title re-split into a `+` chain DIFF.

**Test counts:** the 20 files were run at the base, in a separate base worktree, and at the head, with `--project local --project repo`. Both sides read 671 tests, all passed, with the same count and status sequence per file in 20 of 20. 543 full test names change, and each equals the base name with the planned replacements applied (0 mismatches). No full name repeats on either side.
